summary: Lukasz Gandecki, a lifelong programmer, developed "Books reimagined" after struggling to track characters in a book about Donald Trump's re-election. His initial AI companion app provided contextual character information, images, and page-specific summaries. The project evolved into a sophisticated book experience platform demonstrated with "The Snow Queen" (Polish) and "1984" (English, built for the conference). Key features include a voice assistant with 100ms response time using hold-to-speak interaction, embeddings-based semantic search to find scenes by meaning rather than exact text, and a deep research mode that reads the entire book up to the reader's current position to answer questions. The platform generates scene-appropriate music and character avatars using LLMs for scene analysis, character detection, mood detection, and structured XML metadata output. Gandecki's development philosophy centers on hiding AI from users rather than building chatbot wrappers. AI handles initial drafts while humans curate and refine, since AI cannot judge music quality, graphic aesthetics, or avatar-vibe matching. He describes his iterative approach as "waves of changes," starting with frequent full rewrites that gradually decrease in amplitude until traditional engineering practices like testing and refactoring become viable. For refactoring decisions, he proposes evaluating code by multiplying badness, painfulness, and ease of change, noting that bad code that is never touched should not be refactored. He emphasizes that throwing away AI-generated code feels liberating compared to discarding hand-written code. The player is being open-sourced, enabling others to create Netflix-style book experiences.

sections.title: Origin Story and First Experience
sections.summary: Gandecki introduces himself and explains the project's origin: struggling to track characters in a Trump re-election book, he built a rough AI companion app providing character context, images, and page-specific summaries. He demonstrates the Snow Queen experience with flying sorcerer's apprentices and a shattering mirror.

sections.title: 1984 Demo and Voice Assistant
sections.summary: He demonstrates an English 1984 experience built for the conference. Key feature is a voice assistant with 100ms response time using hold-to-speak. He criticizes existing voice assistants including Siri and Google's demo as terrible, with delays and poor turn-taking. The system can summarize what happened between questions.

sections.title: Search and Deep Research
sections.summary: Covers three search modes: exact search, embeddings-based semantic search for finding scenes by meaning, and deep research that reads the entire book up to the reader's position to answer complex questions like how party propaganda works.

sections.title: Development Methodology
sections.summary: Describes vibe coding in vanilla JS for rapid iteration. Throwing away AI-generated code feels liberating. Uses 'waves of changes' metaphor where rewrite amplitude decreases over time, eventually enabling traditional engineering with tests and refactoring. Proposes refactoring priority as badness × painfulness × ease of change.

sections.title: Design Philosophy: Hiding AI
sections.summary: Advocates hiding AI from users rather than building chatbot wrappers. AI does initial drafts, humans curate the rest. Human judgment is essential for music, graphics, and avatar matching. Simple building blocks connected together create magical experiences. Graphics aid mood and character recall; matching music makes reading feel like watching a movie.

sections.title: Technical Process and Open Source Announcement
sections.summary: Explains the pipeline: LLMs perform scene analysis and character detection, receive overall music themes (e.g., Victorian noir for Sherlock Holmes), combine scene analysis with mood detection for music generation, and output structured XML metadata for character-scene mapping. Announces open-sourcing the player and invites collaboration.
